findings.title: All-groups view permission grants realm-wide group manage
findings.body: GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() returns true when the caller has only the Groups VIEW scope on the all-groups resource (hasPermission(null, VIEW, MANAGE)). requireManage() uses that result, and GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup() calls requireManage() before creating a group. An admin who was granted only view on all groups can therefore create groups (and pass any other no-arg requireManage()/canManage() check). Per-group canManage(GroupModel) correctly requires MANAGE, so this is an escalation specific to the type-level check. The interface javadoc on canManage() documents the same VIEW-or-MANAGE rule and should be corrected with the implementation; view must not imply manage.

findings.title: Group member filter uses authorization resource ids, not group ids
findings.body: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() walks resources with findByType(..., GROUPS) and then calls hasPermission(groupResource.getId(), ...) and granted.add(groupResource.getId()). hasPermission looks the argument up with resourceStore.findByName, but V2 group resources are named with the group id (resolveGroup / getOrCreateResource), while getId() is the authorization resource UUID. The name lookup misses, evaluation falls back to the all-groups resource, and the set stored on the session as UserModel.GROUPS is not a set of group ids. UsersResource and BruteForceUsersResource pass that set into user search, and UsersResource.getUsersCount uses it for counts. If all-groups has view-members/manage-members, every typed resource is treated as granted and search/count are constrained to nonexistent group ids, so members the admin is allowed to see disappear. Per-group grants are not applied as a group-id filter either (and getOrCreateResource never setType(GROUPS), so findByType does not return those resources). The type resource named "Groups" must be skipped; the granted value and the permission lookup must use the group id (resource name).

findings.title: Created group resources are not typed as Groups
findings.body: getOrCreateResource creates a per-object authorization resource and sets scopes, but never calls setType(resourceType). V1 group resources were explicitly typed "Group". GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() discovers candidates only via findByType(server, GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE). Individual group resources created for group permissions therefore never appear, so group-scoped view-members/manage-members permissions cannot drive the user-search group filter even after the id-versus-name bug is fixed. The all-groups resource created in init() is the only one with type Groups.

findings.title: Existing admin-permissions clients are not upgraded with Groups
findings.body: init() returns immediately when realm.getAdminPermissionsClient() is already set, and nothing else creates the new Groups resource type or the manage-membership, manage-members, and view-members scopes. Realms that already enabled admin permissions before this change keep a client whose schema has only the previous resource types and scopes. Creating or evaluating a Groups permission then fails (missing scope / "No scopes found") or NPEs in GroupPermissionsV2.hasPermission when getResourceTypeResource returns null and that null is passed to policyStore.findByResource and resource.getScopes(). There is no migration to add the Groups resource and scopes onto an existing admin-permissions client.

findings.title: Permission resource names are not resolved for groups
findings.body: getResourceName only special-cases the Users resource type (labeling the type resource "All users" and resolving a user id to a username). Groups resources created by this change use the group id as the resource name and do not set a display name to the group name or path. Group permissions therefore fall through to resource.getDisplayName(), so the admin UI shows null or a raw id instead of the group name, and the all-groups resource is not labeled the way all-users is. A missing group also is not reported, unlike a missing user which throws ModelIllegalStateException.

findings.title: Group permission check ignores which resource was granted
findings.body: GroupPermissionsV2.hasPermission accepts any permission in the evaluatePermission result whose scope list intersects the requested scopes. UserPermissionsV2.hasPermission, using the same evaluatePermission API, only accepts a scope when permission.getResourceId() equals the resource under check. Without that filter, a scope granted on a different resource included in the same decision is treated as view, manage, view-members, manage-members, or manage-membership on the group being checked, which over-authorizes group and group-member operations.

findings.title: requireManageMembers javadoc cites the wrong check
findings.body: The javadoc on requireManageMembers says it throws if canManageMembership(GroupModel) is false. The implementation throws when canManageMembers(GroupModel) is false. Callers and implementors following the comment will enforce group-membership management instead of member management.
